subject: Hosted API: PriorityHealth p95 spike — batching backlog investigation
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@priorityhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: High p95/p99 + errors on Hosted API (production)

Aditya / Soojin,

We're seeing a significant regression in p95 and p99 latencies from 02:30–03:30 PT this morning. Throughput for our production workload is roughly stable, but p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.4s and p99 is spiking above 3s. We're also seeing a small uptick in HTTP 5xx rate (~0.7%). This is impacting our nightly ingestion window.

Attached is a small dump from our client-side timing (latency_dump_2026-10-27.csv) and a couple of request IDs we captured: ph-prod-req-00123, ph-prod-req-00129. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your end and provide an initial ETA for mitigation?

We have a hard cutover at 04:30 PT today, so any temporary mitigation would help.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Senior SRE, PriorityHealth

[attachment: latency_dump_2026-10-27.csv]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@priorityhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2026 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95/p99 + errors on Hosted API (production)

Olivia — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. We're investigating immediately. Initial ask: can you confirm roughly what percentage of requests are long-context (>1k tokens) vs short? Also, if you can share 2–3 example request IDs that hit the 3s p99, that will speed up root cause mapping.

Soojin, Markus — assigning to infra on-call to triage batching/queue backpressure. Laura — looping you in for customer comms/ETA. I'll follow up within 30 minutes with a status.

— Aditya
Head of Customer Success (acting), Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@priorityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2026 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High p95/p99 + errors on Hosted API (production)

Aditya / team — quick update from infra triage. We correlated the request IDs Olivia sent and pulled server-side traces. Symptoms: sustained increase in queue depth on the primary inference pool serving PriorityHealth (pool-id: host-pool-12), starting ~02:20 PT. Batching telemetry shows average batch size rising from 6->18 concurrently while worker utilization is steady. That suggests requests are arriving in bursts while kernel latency per token is slightly elevated (likely due to a QAT/quantization kernel recency causing a hot path).

Actions we're taking now:
- Temporarily lower max_batch_size from 32 -> 12 for host-pool-12 (will reduce batching tail but increase per-token compute).
- Flush per-host prefix cache for PriorityHealth to reduce KV cache thrash (happened once in last deploy window).
- Spin up a small hot-standby node group to drain queue pressure (+2 GPUs) — ETA ~25 minutes.

Attaching a brief heap snapshot and the latency dump we pulled server-side. Will update when the hot-standby finishes booting.

— Soojin
SRE, Redwood Inference

[attachment: service_heap_snapshot.txt]

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@priorityhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95/p99 + errors on Hosted API (production)

Thanks Soojin — quick note from our side: the long-context requests are about ~12% of traffic during the window. Screenshots attached from our dashboard show the same p95/p99 pattern around 02:30. We appreciate the temporary scaling. Is there any risk this change will affect output quality for our inference workload? We need to ensure model outputs stay identical.

Olivia

[attachment: ph_screenshot_02_30.png]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@priorityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation & customer-facing plan — PriorityHealth latency spike

Team — moving this to an exec-level action since PriorityHealth is on a tight production cadence today. Summary: p95/p99 regressions caused by batching/queue depth (likely a combination of bursty arrival patterns + an opportunistic kernel path change). Immediate mitigations in flight: reduced max_batch_size, cache flush, +2 GPUs hot-standby.

Customer asks: 1) ETA for full resolution/rollforward plan, 2) whether output quality will change, 3) commitment to a postmortem and corrective rollout.

Proposed comms to customer (short):
- We're actively mitigating; temporary scaling and batching changes are in place to bring latency down within 20–30 minutes.
- We're not changing model weights; only serving parameters (batching/cache), so outputs should be identical. We'll validate on a sample set and confirm.
- We'll deliver a postmortem within 48 hours and a safe rollout plan for any kernel patches.

Laura — please send the updated MAP to Olivia (see attached). Markus / Soojin — please prioritize the validation run (compare outputs before/after batching change on the provided request IDs).

— Aditya

[attachment: mutual_action_plan_priorityhealth.docx]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@priorityhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation & customer-facing plan — PriorityHealth latency spike

Update — mitigation complete. Timeline:
- 10:03 PT: lowered max_batch_size -> immediate reduction in batch build tail. p95 dropped to ~420ms within 4 minutes.
- 10:12 PT: cache flush completed; KV hit-rate stabilized.
- 10:32 PT: hot-standby nodes finished booting; queue depth returned to baseline. p95 now ~240ms, p99 ~520ms. Error rate back to baseline.

Validation: we ran the 6 request IDs Olivia provided through the pre/post comparison harness. Outputs are bit-for-bit identical after batching param change (no model weight or quantization changes). No customer-visible quality delta.

Next steps:
1) Postmortem draft (INF-3129) will be published by EOD tomorrow; root cause currently scoped to kernel selection heuristics + burst pattern.
2) Recommend a conservative change to batch selection heuristics (short-term config change) and a follow-up kernel patch (long-term).
3) Offer PriorityHealth a one-week elevated monitoring window and a 5% usage credit for the incident.

Olivia — please confirm if the compensation offer and plan look acceptable; we'll schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the postmortem when it's ready.

— Markus Klein
VP, Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
